text:
For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d pick the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity and a **2,600 W inverter**, giving you a useful buffer for the smoker’s startup surge and campsite extras. The cited estimate is **two or three 12-hour cooks per charge**; it’s listed at $899 in the search result. ([Source](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

For a **single night on a tighter budget**, the **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W) or **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W) are also sized for an overnight cook, though check current availability and pricing. ([Source](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

Pellet smokers usually draw only about **35–60 W once running**, but the igniter can briefly pull **200–400 W**. Check your smoker’s startup specs, and expect less runtime if you also power lights or charge devices. ([Source](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))
